Seminar Title:

Computational Framework for Classical and Fractional Partial Differential Equations using Polynomial Spectral Collocation and Finite Difference Techniques

Seminar Type:

Synopsis Seminar

Department:

Mathematics

Speaker Name:

Santoshi Tarei ( Rollno : 522ma1001)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Mathematics Dept. Seminar Room

Date and Time:

11 Nov 2026 11:00 AM

Contact:

Ankur Kanaujiya

Abstract:

This thesis focuses on the development and analysis of numerical methods for solving both classical and fractional partial differential equations. The study begins with an introduction to calculus and fractional calculus, followed by a review of existing numerical methods for classical and fractional models. Preliminary concepts, including temporal discretization techniques such as the L1, L1&ndash2, and L2&ndash1&sigma schemes, are presented to approximate time-fractional derivatives effectively. In the first part of the work, spectral collocation methods based on Jaiswal functions, Laguerre functions, and their hybrid forms are developed for solving classical nonlinear partial differential equations. These methods are applied to the FitzHugh&ndashNagumo equation, where pseudo-operational matrices of integration are constructed to transform the governing equations into algebraic systems. Then, the polynomial bases are extended to their fractional counterparts. In particular, fractional-order Jaiswal&ndashLaguerre functions are employed to solve nonlinear equations such as the generalized Newell&ndashWhitehead&ndashSegel equation. Further, the methodology is extended to financial models through compact finite difference schemes developed for the time-fractional Black&ndashScholes equation. By combining spatial compact discretization with L1, L1&minus2, and L2&minus1&sigma temporal schemes, fully discrete numerical methods are constructed. Stability and convergence analyses are performed. The study is further extended to time&ndashspace fractional partial differential equations using fractional Legendre&ndashJaiswal functions, where the governing equations are transformed into algebraic systems through operational and pseudo-operational matrices, and the resulting numerical scheme is shown to be stable and convergent. The approach is then applied to time-fractional convection-diffusion-reaction problems with variable coefficients using fractional Jaiswal&ndashLaguerre functions, particularly for cases where the solution exhibits weak singular behavior at &tau = 0. Furthermore, fractional Gegenbauer-Jaiswal functions are introduced for solving multi-term time-fractional advection-diffusion equations, where improved accuracy and stability are achieved, along with the establishment of error bounds.
